summary.intent: Fix a failing CI build for the TEE worker after recent changes broke TypeScript compilation in the Docker build environment.
summary.outcome: Added an `exclude` for test files in `tee-worker/tsconfig.json` so `tsc` no longer attempts to compile `vitest`-dependent test files during the Docker build. Fix was committed on a `fix(ci)` branch.

repo: The TEE worker does not have `vitest` listed as a dependency (not even a devDependency), so test files using `vitest` imports cannot be compiled by `tsc` in the Docker build context.
The Docker build runs `tsc` directly, meaning any file matched by `tsconfig.json` include globs must have all imports resolvable at build time.
The Desktop App Linux CI failure is a flaky external rate-limit (HTTP 429) during the Tauri build, unrelated to code changes.

code.finding: Originally included `src/**/*` without an exclude, causing test files under `src/__tests__/` to be compiled. Fixed by adding an exclude for test files.
Imports from `vitest` which is not declared in package.json, making it uncompilable in the Docker build environment.

workflow: CI log triage: distinguish code failures from infrastructure/rate-limit failures before attempting fixes.
Branch naming convention used: `fix(ci)` prefix for CI-related fixes.

friction: Had to dig through CI logs across multiple tool calls to isolate the TEE worker error from other job failures.
The Desktop App Linux failure (HTTP 429 rate limit) adds noise to CI runs and could mask real failures.
open_items: The Desktop App Linux CI failure due to an external HTTP 429 rate limit is unresolved and may recur — worth investigating the download source or adding retry logic.
Consider adding `vitest` as a devDependency in the TEE worker if tests are expected to be run in other contexts, or confirm the test setup is intentionally isolated.
